pages.says: The UN climate summit in Antalya ended with no decision at all, the first time since Copenhagen in 2009, after the EU and island states refused a final text with all mention of fossil fuels removed.
pages.weakest: The Chatter box: "Another spotted failed COP years lining up with crises: '2000 2009 2019 Now'"

pages.says: Two Russian missiles and a drone came down inside Poland during a huge strike on Ukraine; Warsaw called it deliberate and Nato said it stood with Poland, but nobody invoked Article 4.
pages.weakest: "After Trump called Putin 'my friend' in Shenzhen, Tusk had posted: 'God, protect us from such friends.'" (Shenzhen is never explained)

pages.says: Lawrence Wong said Singapore can inspect AI chips installed here but has no control over the much larger number only invoiced here and shipped elsewhere, so it will offer Washington information rather than enforcement.
pages.weakest: "Held since No. 168, confirmed: the Economic Survey, with final third-quarter growth, lands Tuesday 24 November at 8am."

pages.says: A good leather sandal comes down to bark-tanned leather and a sewn, replaceable sole, which India's Kolhapuri recipe requires by law, and the page names pairs from about ₹1,231 to ¥55,000.
pages.weakest: "or a Canfora pair from Capri, made since 1946, from about made since 1946, from €100euro;100."
pages.reason: The price paragraph has a broken, repeated sentence that stops the reader cold, and the third paragraph crams Kolhapuri tanning, Birkenstock and Tokyo Sandal construction into one block. Fix the garble, give each build its own sentence or two, and make the deck match the headline.
pages.fixed: Repaired the garbled Canfora price sentence, split the crowded construction paragraph into one paragraph each for the Kolhapuri tan, Birkenstock and Tokyo Sandal, matched the dek to the headline, and restored Prada's ~EUR800 price in the Sceptic.

pages.says: The New York Times reports that China's spy ministry spent two years helping firms get banned Nvidia chips, and a Singapore defendant, Li Ming, is now tied to Megaspeed's former chief.
pages.weakest: "A January 2023 photo shows him as strategy chief of Century Longteng, a company Alice Huang co-founded."

pages.says: A free program called PolyStrata now runs two new AI models on gaming laptops with 8GB graphics cards and claims a big speed advantage, though all the figures are the maker's own.
pages.weakest: "llama.cpp, the most common free engine, still lacks it: pull request 32517 was unmerged on 22 November..."
pages.reason: After a clear second paragraph the page turns into benchmark tables in prose and never says what 56 tokens a second feels like or who should install this. Cut the numbers to the two that matter, compare them to reading speed, and say plainly whether a reader with a gaming laptop should try it.
pages.fixed: Rewrote from paragraph three: cut the benchmark list to two numbers, converted 56 tokens a second to about 40 words a second against a reader's four or five, and said plainly who should try it and who should wait.

pages.says: Xreal's US$1,279 Aura, the first glasses built for Google's Android XR, has bright screens and is comfortable but runs unstable software and has few apps, so reviewers call it a developer kit, and it is not coming to Singapore soon.
pages.weakest: "while noting its 96-degree view beats the Aura's 70" (it is unclear whose 96 degrees)

pages.says: A 1951 pink-gold Patek 1518 with an untouched Spanish calendar made HK$25.1 million, three times its low estimate, while the modern platinum 3990P barely cleared its low: old and untouched beat modern.
pages.weakest: The Chatter box: "The bidding said what forums had not yet posted by press"

pages.says: The new Hunger Games prequel opened to about $120 million in North America and $225 million worldwide, reviving a fading series, though it still has to reach about $375 million to break even.
pages.weakest: "Take That's Dreamers, their tenth studio album, arrived on 20 November ahead of a 31-city tour in 2027."

pages.says: A JAMA study of 3.7 million children links radiation from head CT scans to a small extra risk of brain tumour, about one per 1,266 scans, so parents should ask whether a scan will change what happens next, not refuse one.
pages.weakest: "evidence for cancer from doses below 100 mSv is 'inconclusive'" (switches units from mGy without explaining)

pages.says: A study of 20,910 South Australian pupils shows the move to secondary school itself, not age, lowers wellbeing for about two years, more for girls, so Singapore families facing PSLE results should expect a slow first term.
pages.weakest: "An older Cardiff and UCL study found self-control declined across the move, faster in early-maturing children"

pages.says: US overnight funding markets stayed calm through last week's share sell-off, with reserves steady near $3 trillion, but Fed research says the cushion is thin heading into year-end.
pages.weakest: The Four box: PIMCO Income number row
pages.reason: The article assumes the reader knows what SOFR, the reverse repo and the standing repo window are and why a $1m loan is reassuring. Half the page is a box of fund and bitcoin calls that has nothing to do with the funding story. Explain the plumbing in plain words once, and move or cut the four fund leans.
pages.fixed: Explained SOFR and the standing repo window once in plain words, moved the reverse-repo and Treasury-cash history to p15, rewrote the PIMCO line as words; The Four box kept as a mandated fixture.

pages.says: The Fed's reverse repo, once a $2.55 trillion spare tank of cash, is now nearly empty, so future shocks will hit bank reserves and show up as jumps in overnight rates.
pages.weakest: "Inside the Fund · VWRA's Third Outside The Dollar" box
pages.reason: It restates p14 almost line for line. Make p15 the history and the chart only and drop the repeats, and cut or rebuild the VWRA country-weights box, which is not about liquidity.
pages.fixed: Removed the figures repeated from p14 so the page carries the multi-year history and chart, tied Inside the Fund to liquidity via the dollar, and cut the stray bitcoin aside.

pages.says: Mokuhanga is Japanese woodblock printing done by hand with water-based colour; a Vermont museum is showing nine artists who practise it, and the page traces the residency and conference circle behind it, with Singapore's STPI as the local door.
pages.weakest: "this first page covers the first encounter and the size of the world behind it"

pages.says: Mokuhanga tools are mostly cheap; money matters for the laminated carving knife and the baren, which runs from a $15 starter to a $1,200 hand-made one, and the page prices each item from one Oregon catalogue.
pages.weakest: "aisuki bull-nose chisels run $39.30–62.05 and komasuki U-gouges $48.05–76.30"

pages.says: Japanese woodblock printing split into a team-made school and a do-it-all-yourself school; the team tradition in Tokyo is down to one new trainee carver, while hobbyists gather on Baren Forum.
pages.weakest: "395 : 3" stat box and the table-of-contents opening
pages.reason: The headline and deck are about a single trainee carver, but the opening is a table of contents and the body is mostly the history of the two schools. Lead with the carver shortage and what it threatens, and make the '395 : 3' box readable on its own.
pages.fixed: Led on the Adachi Foundation's carver shortage and why it matters, cut the school history to background, and made the 395 : 3 box readable on its own.

pages.says: Men fitter on a treadmill in middle age later had fewer lung and bowel cancers, but no fewer prostate cancers, and lived longer after a diagnosis, though the study is observational and fitness partly reflects genes and habits.
pages.weakest: "one MET is roughly the gap between a brisk walk and a slow jog"

pages.says: The pick of the coming weeks is Singapore Ballet's Nutcracker at the Esplanade from 9 December, alongside Clockenflap in Hong Kong and Tokyo Comic Con at Makuhari, with prices and booking advice.
pages.weakest: "Still unpriced: Kenshi Yonezu, KATSEYE, Maroon 5, Freya Skye and Mahiru..."

pages.says: Warmhouse Nasi Lemak in Chinatown Complex earned a paying critic's praise for its fried wing and egg at S$5, though not for its rice; a new smash-burger shutter and a Mount Faber café are too new to call.
pages.weakest: "No. 155 noted the mid-October opening; this is the verdict run, from a meal the publication paid for."

pages.says: A top tax-exam candidate's confession that he cheated with a hidden camera and a chatbot led Korea to put stickers on every button of half a million Suneung candidates and cost the education minister his job.
pages.weakest: Unattributed pull quote: "Perhaps because of my age, I don't think I could."

pages.says: Korea has always answered admissions scandals by trusting the anonymous exam more; cheap AI glasses turned a reporter's 28 into an 87, and the Joseon gwageo shows an exam can survive centuries of fraud.
pages.weakest: Unattributed pull quote: "Examinations should assess not only the final answer..."

pages.says: Seoul's responses all seal the room tighter rather than change the test, because the Suneung is what makes the scramble for places look fair, and the essay predicts no end date by 2027 but detectors at next year's sitting.
pages.weakest: "Even the CSAT can no longer be trusted." (CSAT is never explained as the Suneung)
